trust_decision.summary: GenericHub::fromBufferDriver_handler trusts the type, port index and size header from a remote peer's buffer and uses the port as an output-port array index (and the size for raw pointer/length arithmetic) without bounds, connection or length checks; the only guards are FW_ASSERTs.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'unvalidated port index in GenericHub'; the receive handler's first port dispatch (serialOut_out with the wire-supplied port) is the obvious place to look.

fix_sites.entry_point: fromBufferDriver input port (Drv.PassiveBufferDriverClientRecv), fed by the remote buffer driver
fix_sites.module_kind: component handler (header parse: short buffer, type range, size mismatch / rawSize underflow)
component handler -> autocoded serialOut port array
component handler -> bufferOut port array (buffer ownership must be returned on reject)
component handler -> cmdDispOut port array (rawSize-4 underflow, ComBuffer capacity)
cosmetic cast change only, not a security site

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All substantive changes are inside GenericHub::fromBufferDriver_handler (fix.diff:46-289); no other implementation of the hub receive path exists in the tree (only Svc/GenericHub references HUB_TYPE).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could leave the non-PORT branches (event/tlm/cmd-resp) alone because the report names the port index and eventOut/tlmOut are single ports, or leave CMD_DISP length arithmetic alone as 'a size issue, not an index issue'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid messages on valid connected ports must still be delivered, and on HUB_TYPE_BUFFER the buffer must be handed to bufferOut (returned later via bufferOutReturn) on success but returned to the driver on reject; an over-broad fix that always returns the buffer double-frees, one that drops instead of returning leaks the driver buffer. Unconnected ports must be skipped without asserting.

O6_input_shapes: port >= number of output ports for each of 6 message types (fix.diff:178, 188, 214, 233, 257, 278)
valid index but unconnected port (same lines, isConnected_* checks)
CMD_DISP payload smaller than the U32 context or larger than ComBuffer::SERIALIZED_SIZE (fix.diff:244)
truncated per-type body (event/tlm/cmd-resp fields fail to deserialize) (fix.diff:202-211, 226-232, 270-276)

O7_producer.where: Svc/GenericHub/GenericHub.cpp:31-46 (send_data on the peer hub writes type, port, length-prefixed data)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A router variant that selects an output port array index from a field of the received frame context or packet header instead of always using index 0.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: FprimeRouter already dispatches uplinked data by a received field (APID) and deliberately skips isConnected on the command path, so a multi-port extension indexed by a wire value is a natural maintainer change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Remote-command path selecting the RemoteCmd port index from data in the command packet rather than from the input portNum.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CmdSplitter sits next to GenericHub in the remote-command topology (GenericHub.fpp:69-73), and routing by packet content is a plausible feature.

O9_family: CWE-129 improper validation of array index (port index from remote peer) with related length-underflow; out-of-range index hits autocoded port arrays / FW_ASSERT

O10_build.project_tests: Svc/GenericHub/test/ut (GenericHubTester.cpp, GenericHubTestMain.cpp), round-trip of every message type between two hub instances

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a `port < getNum_serialOut_OutputPorts()` check before serialOut_out only, leaving the other five dispatches, the header-length underflow and the CMD_DISP length arithmetic as is.

out_of_scope_notes: Svc/GenericHub/GenericHub.cpp:65-72 sender-side cmdDispIn buffer is ComBuffer::SERIALIZED_SIZE but also has to hold the U32 context; a full ComBuffer would trip the assert (local, not wire-driven).
Svc/GenericHub/GenericHub.cpp:57-60 bufferOutReturn returns a buffer whose data pointer was shifted at :131; the driver gets back a rebased buffer (ownership nuance, not pursued).
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell available); fprime is mid-sized, likely well over 5 MB and well under 1.5 GB.
The behaviour of autocoded *_out functions for out-of-range portNum (assumed FW_ASSERT then array index) is generated at build time and was not read.

Near single_site: substantive changes are confined to one function (fromBufferDriver_handler) but at several places, so the single_site definition does not strictly hold; with no O2/O8 this host behaves much like one.
fix commit f972bed2 is a CI workflow change only, so it is not counted as a source change.
O9_dos: true because the pre-fix failure mode on FSW is an assert/abort, and in builds with asserts disabled an out-of-bounds port-array access.
Searched Svc/ and Drv/ for other wire-derived output-port indices and found none (all other *_out(portNum...) calls use the local input portNum).
